commits.edited_message:
ar: Always skip all special entry bytes

The special file entries / and // are supposed to be properly padded,
but don't implicitly rely on it. Use archive_read_format_ar_skip
instead which takes care of possible padding bytes.

Also pass the filename table size into ar_parse_gnu_filename_table()
explicitly instead of having it re-read ar->strtab_size, so the
parser works from the same value the caller just finished validating.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
(cherry picked from commit 918c0d28235910656e0048799ae030e38a7461ba)

ar: Improve error messages

Always use the term filename table and merge filename table size
checks into one.

Also round the size passed to ar_parse_gnu_filename_table() up to
the even boundary GNU ar always pads the table to, in case the
declared size in the header doesn't already account for it.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
(cherry picked from commit 2f2520510f2257dfe7207b757a652f6ef05b94b6)

coupling: The defect is split across two consecutive real commits in libarchive/archive_read_support_format_ar.c, both touching the GNU ar filename-table ('//' entry) handling. Commit f4d4ee5 ('ar: Always skip all special entry bytes') is edited to additionally refactor ar_parse_gnu_filename_table() to take the table size as an explicit parameter instead of re-reading ar->strtab_size internally -- a behavior-preserving change on its own (the call site passes the same strtab_size value that was just used for the malloc(), the __archive_read_ahead(), and the memcpy()). Commit 9d1cb1c ('ar: Improve error messages') is edited to, alongside its real change (merging the two size-validation checks into one), also change the call site to pass strtab_size + (strtab_size % 2) -- 'defensively rounding up to the even size GNU ar always pads the table to'. Neither edit is wrong in isolation: f4d4ee5's diff only threads an existing, already-validated value through as a new parameter (textually identical value, same hunk shows the parameter and the unchanged argument); 9d1cb1c's diff is a small, localized change at the call site (a few lines near the merged size check) that does not re-show the malloc()/read_ahead()/memcpy() lines (which sit ~15-20 lines above, in a part of the function neither commit's diff touches), so there is nothing in either hunk that looks inconsistent by itself. Only by tracing the whole function -- noting that the buffer is malloc'd and filled with exactly strtab_size bytes (unrounded, from the untouched code both commits leave alone), while the parser now receives strtab_size rounded up to even -- does the off-by-one become visible: when the attacker-controlled declared table size is odd, the parser is told the table is one byte larger than the heap allocation, and both its internal loop (`*(p + 1)` with p one short of the claimed end) and its final `ar->strtab[size - 1] = '\0'` read/write one byte past the allocation. Reverting either commit's call-site argument back to plain strtab_size removes the bug; reverting only the other one (while keeping the rounding) does not, since the rounding is what actually introduces the wrong value -- but the rounding is only expressible at all because f4d4ee5's parameterization made the function trust a caller-supplied size instead of its own single source of truth (ar->strtab_size, which stays correct throughout). A reviewer must look at the malloc/read_ahead/memcpy sizing (untouched context, not part of either diff) together with both commits' call-site edits to see that the parser's notion of the table size has silently diverged from the buffer's real size.
